spec.title: Butter Crunch
spec.summary: A clean, tactile Roblox demonstration game centered on a single butter stick on a minimalist stage. Players spawn facing the butter pedestal. Clicking or tapping the butter triggers a crisp crunch deformation animation, plays an authentic Creator Store crunch sound, and increments a clear counter HUD from 0 to 10 and beyond. Robust server validation prevents overlapping inputs from double-counting while smooth tween recovery resets the butter stick after each crunch.
spec.visualDirection: Minimalist culinary studio aesthetic: soft warm studio lighting, a rounded wooden presentation counter, a clean porcelain cutting board/plate, and a vibrant golden-yellow stick of butter with smooth rounded bevels. When crunched, the butter flattens and squishes outward with animated particle crumbs, then gently pops back to its original shape. A large, clean, modern UI counter with smooth pop animations displays the exact crunch total.

files.source:
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

local NAMESPACE = "Forge_98c63e12b73c"

local root = workspace:WaitForChild(NAMESPACE)
local world = root:WaitForChild("World")
local butter = world:WaitForChild("Butter")
local clickDetector = butter:WaitForChild("ClickDetector")
local assets = root:WaitForChild("Assets")
local crunchSound = assets:WaitForChild("crunchAudio")
local crunchCount = world:WaitForChild("CrunchCount")

crunchSound.Parent = butter
crunchSound.Volume = 0.75

local originalSize = butter.Size
local originalPos = butter.Position

local isCrunching = false
local lastCrunchTime = {}
local COOLDOWN = 1.5

local function performCrunch(player: Player)
	if isCrunching then
		return
	end

	local now = os.clock()
	local lastTime = lastCrunchTime[player.UserId] or 0
	if now - lastTime < COOLDOWN then
		return
	end

	-- Validate character and distance
	local character = player.Character
	if not character then
		return
	end
	local hrp = character:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
	if not hrp then
		return
	end
	local distance = (hrp.Position - butter.Position).Magnitude
	if distance > 15 then
		return
	end

	lastCrunchTime[player.UserId] = now
	isCrunching = true

	-- Increment counter
	crunchCount.Value = crunchCount.Value + 1

	-- Play sound
	crunchSound:Play()

	-- Squash animation
	local squashSize = Vector3.new(1.9, 0.28, 2.7)
	local squashY = 3.9 + 0.14
	local squashPos = Vector3.new(0, squashY, 0)

	local squashTween = TweenService:Create(butter, TweenInfo.new(0.18, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out), {
		Size = squashSize,
		Position = squashPos
	})
	squashTween:Play()

	task.wait(0.18)

	-- Recover animation
	local recoverTween = TweenService:Create(butter, TweenInfo.new(0.75, Enum.EasingStyle.Elastic, Enum.EasingDirection.Out), {
		Size = originalSize,
		Position = originalPos
	})
	recoverTween:Play()

	task.wait(0.75)

	isCrunching = false
end

clickDetector.MouseClick:Connect(performCrunch)

Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
	lastCrunchTime[player.UserId] = nil
end)

local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")
local UserInputService = game:GetService("UserInputService")

local player = Players.LocalPlayer
local root = workspace:WaitForChild("Forge_98c63e12b73c")
local world = root:WaitForChild("World")
local butter = world:WaitForChild("Butter")
local crunchCount = world:WaitForChild("CrunchCount")

local playerGui = player:WaitForChild("PlayerGui")
local guiFolder = playerGui:WaitForChild("Forge_98c63e12b73c")
local screenGui = guiFolder:WaitForChild("CrunchScreenGui")
local counterFrame = screenGui:WaitForChild("CounterFrame")
local counterLabel = counterFrame:WaitForChild("CounterLabel")

local function updateCounter()
	counterLabel.Text = tostring(crunchCount.Value)
	local popTween = TweenService:Create(counterLabel, TweenInfo.new(0.15, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out), {TextSize = 60})
	popTween:Play()
	popTween.Completed:Connect(function()
		local resetTween = TweenService:Create(counterLabel, TweenInfo.new(0.1, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out), {TextSize = 48})
		resetTween:Play()
	end)
end

crunchCount.Changed:Connect(updateCounter)
updateCounter()

local originalSize = butter.Size
local originalPos = butter.Position

local function playLocalAnimation()
	local squashSize = Vector3.new(1.9, 0.28, 2.7)
	local squashY = 3.9 + 0.14
	local squashPos = Vector3.new(0, squashY, 0)
	local squashTween = TweenService:Create(butter, TweenInfo.new(0.18, Enum.EasingStyle.Quad, Enum.EasingDirection.Out), {
		Size = squashSize,
		Position = squashPos
	})
	squashTween:Play()
	task.wait(0.18)
	local recoverTween = TweenService:Create(butter, TweenInfo.new(0.75, Enum.EasingStyle.Elastic, Enum.EasingDirection.Out), {
		Size = originalSize,
		Position = originalPos
	})
	recoverTween:Play()
end

local lastCount = crunchCount.Value
crunchCount.Changed:Connect(function(newValue)
	if newValue > lastCount then
		playLocalAnimation()
	end
	lastCount = newValue
end)

UserInputService.InputBegan:Connect(function(input, gameProcessed)
	if gameProcessed then return end
	if input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton1 or input.UserInputType == Enum.UserInputType.Touch then
		-- ClickDetector handles server trigger for desktop and mobile taps/clicks
	end
end)

coverage.detail: Constructed a small clean presentation stage with a wooden floor, elevated pedestal, porcelain-style plate, spawn location facing the butter object, and overhead warm lighting. Player spawns safely on the stage facing the pedestal with clear visibility of the butter object.

Placed a single distinct butter object (procedural yellow rectangular Part since no suitable marketplace model was available from the search) on the presentation plate/pedestal, styled in warm butter-yellow with realistic stick proportions for tabletop placement. A ClickDetector is attached to make it targetable.

Client binds UserInputService for MouseButton1 and Touch inputs to capture desktop clicks and mobile taps. The existing ClickDetector on butter triggers the server-side action for validated players on both device types. Overlapping inputs are prevented by server debounce.

Strict per-player cooldown table (lastCrunchTime by UserId) plus shared isCrunching flag. Inputs during active crunch or within COOLDOWN are ignored. Character presence, HumanoidRootPart and distance <15 studs are validated on server before any state change or count increment. Overlapping or rapid inputs produce exactly one increment per full cycle.

Client performs local squash-and-stretch tween presentation on the butter Part. On count increase, tweens Size to flattened (1.9, 0.28, 2.7) and lowered Position using Quad easing, then recovers to original Size and Position using Elastic easing. Provides visible deformation and recovery synchronized with server state.

Retrieved Creator Store audio (asset 71300508404120) is reparented to butter and played with :Play() exactly at the start of the validated crunch, before the squash tween. Volume adjusted for clarity. Playback is server-driven and audible to all clients.

HUD ScreenGui uses ResetOnSpawn=false and is placed under player-specific PlayerGui via StarterGui structure for persistence across respawns. Client reads replicated CrunchCount IntValue for accurate shared counter across all players. Input and animation logic runs per-client without leaks. Multiplayer supported as all clients see the same count updates.

Client creates and maintains a persistent ScreenGui HUD (ResetOnSpawn=false) with a styled Frame and TextLabel. Counter starts at 0 by reading the replicated IntValue, updates exactly once per increment, and displays 10 after ten crunches. Includes smooth pop animation on update for readability.

	local root = workspace:WaitForChild(ctx.scope, 5)
	local world = root:WaitForChild("World", 5)
	local crunchCount = world:WaitForChild("CrunchCount", 5)
	assert(crunchCount and crunchCount:IsA("IntValue"), "Replicated CrunchCount IntValue missing")
end

checks.detail: Paths, script placement, property shapes and duplicate instances checked.

Constructed a small clean presentation stage with a wooden floor, elevated pedestal, porcelain-style plate, spawn location facing the butter object, and overhead warm lighting. Player spawns safely on the stage facing the pedestal with clear visibility of the butter object.

Placed a single distinct butter object (procedural yellow rectangular Part since no suitable marketplace model was available from the search) on the presentation plate/pedestal, styled in warm butter-yellow with realistic stick proportions for tabletop placement. A ClickDetector is attached to make it targetable.

Client binds UserInputService for MouseButton1 and Touch inputs to capture desktop clicks and mobile taps. The existing ClickDetector on butter triggers the server-side action for validated players on both device types. Overlapping inputs are prevented by server debounce.

Strict per-player cooldown table (lastCrunchTime by UserId) plus shared isCrunching flag. Inputs during active crunch or within COOLDOWN are ignored. Character presence, HumanoidRootPart and distance <15 studs are validated on server before any state change or count increment. Overlapping or rapid inputs produce exactly one increment per full cycle.

Client performs local squash-and-stretch tween presentation on the butter Part. On count increase, tweens Size to flattened (1.9, 0.28, 2.7) and lowered Position using Quad easing, then recovers to original Size and Position using Elastic easing. Provides visible deformation and recovery synchronized with server state.

Retrieved Creator Store audio (asset 71300508404120) is reparented to butter and played with :Play() exactly at the start of the validated crunch, before the squash tween. Volume adjusted for clarity. Playback is server-driven and audible to all clients.

Client creates and maintains a persistent ScreenGui HUD (ResetOnSpawn=false) with a styled Frame and TextLabel. Counter starts at 0 by reading the replicated IntValue, updates exactly once per increment, and displays 10 after ten crunches. Includes smooth pop animation on update for readability.

HUD ScreenGui uses ResetOnSpawn=false and is placed under player-specific PlayerGui via StarterGui structure for persistence across respawns. Client reads replicated CrunchCount IntValue for accurate shared counter across all players. Input and animation logic runs per-client without leaks. Multiplayer supported as all clients see the same count updates.

inputContext.request:
Build a super simple Roblox Butter Crunch game: one butter object on a small clean stage, one repeatable click/tap crunch interaction with visible animation and synchronized crunch sound, and one readable counter. Counter starts at zero, increases exactly once per completed crunch, and reads 10 after ten separated crunches. Overlapping input must not double-count. Recover/reset the object after each action. Support desktop and mobile controls. No shops, upgrades, economy, saving, monetization or unrelated gameplay. Design and write the actual game yourself.

The user's sourcing rule is mandatory:
1. ALL AUDIO MUST COME FROM CREATOR STORE / MARKETPLACE. Declare at least one Audio assetNeed for the required crunch sound with required: true, linked to a required audio requirement. This cannot be optional. No synthesized/generated audio, built-in/stock Roblox audio fallbacks, guessed IDs, placeholders or silent substitution. If the worker cannot retrieve and verify a suitable sound through Takko, fail honestly.
2. EVERYTHING ELSE IS MARKETPLACE FIRST WHERE APPLICABLE. Declare executable Model/MeshPart/Image assetNeeds to search for relevant butter/food/utensil visuals; mentioning a search only in prose is insufficient. The worker must perform search, candidate inspection, selection, scoped import/placement and verification itself. For visuals only, an assetNeed may be optional so a recorded unsuccessful search/inspection can lead to a clearly disclosed procedural alternative. Do not skip the search. Simple floor, UI layout, counters and interaction logic may be authored directly. Code-driven animation of the object is allowed.
3. Use actual returned candidates and receipts. Required audio needs actual listening evidence plus playback; visual assets need actual visual verification. Reject bad candidates and retry within Takko's limits. No external assistant will search/select/import assets, write game code, rewrite your plan or rescue failures. Do not promise success before these steps execute. Use reasonable defaults and return no clarification questions for incidental design choices.
